text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore government says changes to Group Representation Constituencies will not reduce minority representation in Parliament.
- Singapore working with China on ways of crafting tax incentives for high-tech investments and longer-term targets for flagship joint venture.
- North Korean soldier bleeding from gunshot wounds crawls into South Korean territory in dramatic defection.
- Acting Prime Minister Tony Tan tells Singaporeans not to vote for opposition that tries to mislead.
- Volume of private property transactions is up after a sharp decline following the May 15 curbs on speculation.
- London analysts say U.S. Fairmont Hotel Management Ltd likely to put in a bid for Lonrho plc's Princess hotel chain.
- Hongkong-based mould base maker Lung Kee Metal Holdings will postpone the launch of its initial public offering.
- Amcol Holdings' single largest shareholder, Henry Pribadi, said to put his 17.9 percent stake in the company up for sale.
- Analysts says New Zealand's financial markets will remain calm when they reopen on Monday as the deadlocked weekend polls were in line with expectations.
- Former managing director of Scotts Holdings, Rafiq Jumabhoy, denies making general offer for service apartment operator.
- Japan's rising property transactions indicate five-year-long slump in property and land markets is coming to an end.
- The International Monetary Fund and World Bank are to launch a major initiative with other international and regional organisations to help prevent global banking crises.
- Listed DBS Bank will hold its biennial investment conference in Hongkong, outside of Singapore for the first time. -- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
